title: Finite type of top higher direct image for a proper morphism
statement: Let $h:X\to Y$ be a proper morphism of schemes [def-pc-scheme, def-weil-proper-morphism], and let $d\geq0$ be an integer. Suppose every scheme-theoretic fibre $X_y$ [def-pc-scheme-fibre] has Krull dimension at most $d$ [def-kun-topological-krull-dimension]. If $H$ is a quasi-coherent $\mathcal O_X$-module of finite type [pqf-def-coherent], then $R^d h_*H$ [pqf-def-cohomology] is a quasi-coherent $\mathcal O_Y$-module of finite type. No Noetherian, flatness or finite-presentation hypothesis is imposed.

source.place: Tag 0EX4, lemma-proper-top-cohomology-finite-type. The output module is on Y; the O_X in the source conclusion is a typographical error.

proof.text: A proper morphism is quasi-compact by finite type and quasi-separated by separatedness. Hence $R^dh_*H$ is quasi-coherent. For an affine open $V\subseteq Y$, higher direct images restrict to those of $h_V:h^{-1}V\to V$. This morphism is proper by base change, its fibres are the original fibres, and the restricted module remains quasi-coherent and finite type (restrict its local generators). Since finite type is local on $Y$, it suffices to prove the claim with $Y=\operatorname{Spec}R$. Such a $Y$ is quasi-compact and quasi-separated; so is $X$, by permanence for quasi-compact and quasi-separated morphisms. The case of an empty target or source is immediate, with zero output.

Over $Y=\operatorname{Spec}R$, affine-base cohomology identifies $\Gamma(Y,R^dh_*H)$ with $H^d(X,H)$. This identification is $R$-linear: for $r\in R$, apply its stated naturality to multiplication by $h^*r$ on $H$; the two induced maps are scalar multiplication by $r$. The affine finite-type criterion therefore says that it suffices to show that $H^d(X,H)$ is a finitely generated $R$-module. We use the same natural $R$-linear affine-base identification for all later proper morphisms over $Y$.

source.place: Tag 0EX4, first paragraph, with Tags 01XK and 01PB

proof.text: Write $X=\varprojlim_i X_i$ over $Y$ using proper closed-immersion approximation: each $h_i:X_i\to Y$ is proper and finitely presented, and every transition and projection $a_i:X\to X_i$ is a closed immersion. Apply the fibre-dimension limit lemma with the constant base system $Y$: the base transitions are identities, hence affine; the stages are finite type; and its closed comparison maps are exactly the given transition maps. It yields an index $i$ such that all fibres of $h_i$ have dimension at most $d$. Fix this index and write $a=a_i$, $Z=X_i$, $g=h_i$, so $h=g\circ a$.

The closed immersion $a:X\hookrightarrow Z$ is finite: over each affine open of $Z$ it is $\operatorname{Spec}(B/I)\to\operatorname{Spec}B$, and $B/I$ is generated by $1$ as a $B$-module. Thus $G=a_*H$ is quasi-coherent and finite type by finite pushforward, without a Noetherian assumption. Since $a$ is affine, $R^qa_*H=0$ for $q>0$. The module-sheaf category on $X$ has enough injectives. Apply the base-linear acyclic Leray comparison to $a$ followed by $g:Z\to\operatorname{Spec}R$ to obtain $H^d(Z,G)\cong H^d(X,H)$ as $R$-modules. Consequently the finiteness problem reduces to a proper finitely presented morphism over an affine base with fibres of dimension at most $d$ and a finite-type quasi-coherent coefficient module. Rename these $h:X\to Y$ and $H$.

source.place: Tag 0EX4, second paragraph; affine vanishing and base-linear Leray, Tag 089W

proof.text: Express $H=\varinjlim_\alpha G_\alpha$ with each $G_\alpha$ finitely presented. These modules are quasi-coherent. Choose a finite affine cover $X=\bigcup_{j=1}^m U_j$ and finitely many sections generating $H|_{U_j}$ for each $j$. Sections on $U_j$ commute with this directed colimit, so each chosen generator lifts to some $G_\alpha(U_j)$. Directedness gives one index $\alpha$ above the finitely many indices. At that index $G_\alpha\to H$ contains every chosen generator on every $U_j$ and is therefore surjective. Put $H'=G_\alpha$ and $K=\ker(H'\to H)$. This is the finite-generator argument for the quotient used in the source; no surjectivity of the original transition maps is needed.

source.place: Tag 0EX4, third paragraph; Properties Tag 086M, lemma-finite-directed-colimit-surjective-maps, finite-generator argument

proof.text: The kernel $K$ is quasi-coherent. The proper fibre-dimension vanishing theorem gives $R^{d+1}h_*K=0$, hence $H^{d+1}(X,K)=0$ by affine-base cohomology. The long exact sequence of right-derived global sections for $0\to K\to H'\to H\to0$ now gives a surjection $H^d(X,H')\twoheadrightarrow H^d(X,H)$. Here the module-sheaf category has enough injectives, and global sections is additive and left exact because it computes kernels sectionwise. The map is $R$-linear, being induced by a module map. Images of a finite generating set generate a quotient. It remains to prove finiteness for the finitely presented coefficient module $H'$.

source.place: Tag 0EX4, third paragraph; Tag 0E7D and the long exact derived sequence

proof.text: Use the inverse system $Y_\lambda=\operatorname{Spec}R_\lambda$, indexed by the finitely generated $\mathbf Z$-subalgebras of $R$, with limit $Y$. It is a small nonempty directed system (adjoin the union of two finite generating sets for an upper bound). Regard it as the Noetherian approximation of $Y$. Proper finitely presented descent gives a proper finitely presented model $h_0:X_0\to Y_0$ with $X\cong X_0\times_{Y_0}Y$. For $\lambda\ge0$ take $X_\lambda=X_0\times_{Y_0}Y_\lambda$. These morphisms remain proper and finitely presented. The system has limit $X$: a compatible cone into $X_\lambda$ is precisely a map into $X_0$ and a compatible cone into $Y_\lambda$ agreeing over $Y_0$, hence a unique map into the fibre product. Its comparison maps are isomorphisms, hence closed immersions. The fibre-dimension limit lemma therefore supplies a stage $j$ whose fibres all have dimension at most $d$.

source.place: Tag 0EX4, fourth paragraph, scheme descent and fibre-dimension bound; Tags 01ZM, 081F and 05M5

proof.text: Apply finite-presentation module descent to $H'$ on the cartesian system just obtained. It gives a later index $k\ge j$ and a finitely presented quasi-coherent module $H_k$ on $X_k$ with $H'\cong b_X^*H_k$, where $b_X:X\to X_k$ lies over $b:Y\to Y_k$. Each $Y_\lambda$ is Noetherian because it is of finite type over $\operatorname{Spec}\mathbf Z$, and each $X_\lambda$ is Noetherian by finite type. Thus the descent theorem's Noetherian affine-base hypotheses hold. Finite presentation implies finite type directly from a local finite presentation, so $H_k$ is coherent by the locally Noetherian criterion. At the earlier dimension-bounded stage $j$, proper fibre-dimension vanishing gives vanishing above $d$ for every quasi-coherent module. Both stage schemes are qcqs by properness over an affine scheme. Clause (a) of top-degree base change passes this vanishing to $h_k:X_k\to Y_k$. Rename $k$ as $j$; subsequent steps use this vanishing, without needing a new fibre-dimension assertion.

source.place: Tag 0EX4, fourth paragraph, module descent and coherence; Tag 01ZR, lemma-descend-modules-finite-presentation; Tag 01XZ

proof.text: For the proper Noetherian-stage morphism $h_j:X_j\to Y_j$, coherence of higher direct images gives $N=R^dh_{j,*}H_j$ coherent, hence quasi-coherent and finite type. Both stage schemes are quasi-compact and quasi-separated, and vanishing above $d$ holds for every quasi-coherent coefficient module as arranged in the preceding step. Clause (c) of top-degree base change, with the first base change the identity and the further one $b:Y\to Y_j$, yields $b^*N\cong R^dh_*H'$. The pullback is quasi-coherent. On affine opens its sections are a tensor extension of those of $N$; if $n_1,\ldots,n_t$ generate the latter, $n_1\otimes1,\ldots,n_t\otimes1$ generate the extension. The affine finite-type criterion therefore shows that $b^*N$, and hence $R^dh_*H'$, is finite type. Its sections over the affine target are finite over $R$; the identification of step 2 gives finiteness of $H^d(X,H')$.

source.place: Tag 0EX4, fourth paragraph and conclusion; Tag 0EX3, lemma-top-cohomology-functor; Tags 02O5 and 02O6

proof.text: Step 6 gives finiteness for the original finite-type coefficient in the finitely presented case. Step 4 transfers it back across the closed immersion, and step 2 turns it into finite type of the higher direct image over every affine open of $Y$. Step 1 then glues the assertion. This proves the stated quasi-coherence and finite type over $Y$.
